intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Iran claims drone attacks on US forces in Gulf
items.text: Iran's army has said it launched drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, where US forces are based. Kuwait said its air defences engaged hostile drones but did not confirm a hit. Bahrain said it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks early on Wednesday and urged residents to take shelter. A day earlier, US officials said American aircraft had struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island. Talks between the two countries remain stalled over safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

gloss.intercept: to stop something before it reaches its target
gloss.shelter: to go somewhere safe from danger
gloss.air defences: weapons and systems used to stop attacks from the sky
gloss.strike: a military attack, usually from the air

items.title: Putin and Xi meet at APEC summit in China
items.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday. The meeting took place a day before three-way talks with US President Donald Trump on Thursday. Mr Putin said economic pressure on other countries was a thing of the past. He added that he expected the talks with Mr Trump to be useful. Separately, the Quad group of countries held its first leaders' meeting in more than two years in Manila.

gloss.on the sidelines: at the edge of a main event, in separate smaller meetings
gloss.summit: an important meeting between leaders of countries
gloss.economic coercion: using economic pressure to force another country to act

items.title: Mauritius threatens legal action over Chagos Islands
items.text: Mauritius has said it will start a legal challenge in the New Year unless Britain sets out a clear plan to approve the Chagos Islands agreement by December. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam said he would prefer the deal to come into force without a legal process. The agreement would hand control of the islands to Mauritius, while the joint US-UK base on Diego Garcia stays open. Progress on the law needed to carry it out was paused in April. Andy Burnham met Mr Ramgoolam earlier this month.

gloss.legal challenge: a formal attempt to stop or change something through the courts
gloss.ratify: to approve a treaty officially so that it becomes valid
gloss.roadmap: a plan showing the steps needed to reach a goal
gloss.come into force: to start to apply as a law or agreement

items.title: England win Nations League group in Madrid
items.text: England have finished top of their Nations League group after beating Spain in Madrid on Sunday. They had already reached the knockout stage before the match. The win means England go into the quarter-finals as group winners. The last-eight ties are due to be played in March. Sky Sports said the draw would decide which of the other qualified teams England will face.

gloss.progress: to move forward to the next stage
gloss.knockout stage: the part of a competition where losing teams go out
gloss.quarter-final: one of the four matches before the semi-finals
gloss.draw: the process that decides which teams play each other
gloss.qualify: to earn a place in a competition

items.title: Zverev reaches ATP Finals semi-finals in Turin
items.text: Alexander Zverev beat American Ben Shelton 6-2, 7-6 (4) on Tuesday to reach the semi-finals of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German is the top seed in the John McEnroe Group. In the same group, France's Arthur Fils beat Spain's Rafael Jodar 4-6, 6-2, 6-2 for his first win at the event. In the doubles, Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic beat the defending champions, Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten. The tournament runs until 22 November.

gloss.seed: a player ranked high enough to be kept apart from other top players in the draw
gloss.defending champion: the winner of the previous year's event
gloss.round robin: a format where every player plays all the others in a group

items.title: Google denies widespread Gmail outage
items.text: Google has said it is not seeing evidence of a broad Gmail disruption, after users reported problems on Tuesday. The outage-tracking site Downdetector logged more than 2,800 reports by midday in New York. Most of them were about receiving email. Google's own Workspace Status Dashboard showed no active Gmail problem at 1.45pm Eastern time. A Google spokesperson told Anadolu that the company was not currently seeing a service disruption of that kind.

gloss.outage: a period when a service does not work
gloss.disruption: something that stops a system from working normally
gloss.spokesperson: a person who speaks officially for a company or group

items.title: Study finds the heart ages unevenly
items.text: Scientists say the heart does not age in the way they had thought. New research suggests that inflammation and scarring build up mainly in the heart valves and the major blood vessels, rather than in the heart muscle itself. The findings, reported by ScienceDaily on 16 November, could change how doctors look for early signs of age-related heart disease. The work also raises questions about how treatments should be targeted in older patients.

gloss.inflammation: swelling and redness in the body, often caused by injury or infection
gloss.scarring: marks of damaged tissue that stay after healing
gloss.valve: a part that controls the flow of liquid, such as blood in the heart
gloss.target: to aim a treatment at a particular thing

items.title: Nvidia revenue doubles in first report without Huang
items.text: Nvidia has reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, which was higher than analysts expected. It is the first earnings report since co-founder Jensen Huang left his role as chief executive. Board chair Harvey Jones said there were no plans to bring him back. Mr Huang has apologised in his first public statement and said he would return if the board decided it was in the company's best interest. He has also agreed to speak to three House committees.

gloss.revenue: the total money a company earns from sales
gloss.earnings report: a company's official statement of its profits and sales
gloss.beat expectations: to do better than experts predicted
gloss.reinstate: to give someone their old job or position back
gloss.board: the group of people who direct a company

items.title: GTA VI launches at midnight on PS5 and Xbox
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI goes on sale on Thursday 19 November at midnight local time, according to Rockstar. It is out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and no PC release is planned for now. In the US the Standard Edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition $99.99. Digital preorders opened for preloading on 10 November, and Rockstar says the game needs up to 212 GB of free space. Preloading does not give early access.

gloss.preload: to download a game before its official release so you can play when it launches
gloss.edition: a particular version of a product
gloss.free space: storage on a device that is not yet used
gloss.early access: permission to use something before its official release

items.title: GTA VI preorders reach about $1.45 billion
items.text: Take-Two has reported strong demand for Grand Theft Auto VI before its launch, 13 years after the last main game in the series. Sensor Tower estimated 14.9 million digital preorders by 16 November, worth about $1.45 billion. The research firm Newzoo has projected global sales of between $3.25 billion and $5.2 billion in the first week. The game launches at midnight on Thursday, after a long marketing campaign by Rockstar Games.

gloss.preorder: an order for a product before it is released
gloss.estimate: to give a rough figure based on available information
gloss.demand: how much people want to buy something
gloss.campaign: a planned set of activities to promote something
